summary: Buck Island Light on an island about two miles south-west of St. Thomas: built by Denmark (1913 or 1916), lit 1 August 1916 per a government notice; rebuilt 2023.

light.note: Historic light: 1916 notice gives a square white tower 9 m high, three flashes every twenty seconds, flame about 38 m (125 ft) above the sea, visible about 17.5 nautical miles. The 1927 inventory gives the focal plane as 125 ft and acetylene illumination.

structures.name: historic light
structures.type: square steel tower, Danish Colonial style
structures.note: Built 1913 per Kelley (2003, via Rowlett) and the Rowlett directory; the 1916 notice says erected in 1916. Kelley and Rowlett give 25 ft (7.6-8 m) high; the notice gives 9 m (about 30 ft). The sources do not explain the difference. Inactive since the mid-1990s.

structures.type: steel tower beside the old light
structures.note: Built in the mid-1990s about 50 ft north-west of the old light (Kelley). The Free Press says an 'old tower' on the island was toppled by Hurricane Irma in 2017; no source names which tower, so identifying it as this one is an inference (Rowlett: the 2023 tower is 'almost identical to an older tower built in the 1990s'). Replaced in 2023.

Active aid to navigation; rebuilt April 2023; 3,500-pound tower delivered in parts by helicopter sling load and assembled on the island; approx. 40 ft (12 m) per Rowlett, focal plane 139 ft (42 m) per Rowlett. Rowlett says it is located adjacent to the historic light.

staffing.note: 1916 notice: unguarded. 1927 inventory: one keeper upstairs and one laborer in the basement of the dwelling.

facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (island and historic light); U.S. Coast Guard (active light)

access.note: The refuge is closed to the public as a bird sanctuary; the old light and its tower are closed. The Society's record gives Open to Public: No.

events.note: Built by the Danish government in Danish Colonial style (Kelley, 2003, via Rowlett); the USLHS record also gives 1913. The 1916 notice says erected in 1916.
Danish government notice dated 8 June 1916: lit 1 August 1916.
Listed among lights established in the fiscal year 1918 by the Commissioner of Lighthouses.
The Harbor Board of St. Thomas conveyed the lighthouse and improvements to the United States on 29 July 1919.
Changed from oil to acetylene, $1,000, under the general appropriations of fiscal 1922.
Coast Guard declared the light station excess property; GSA transferring it to the Fish and Wildlife Service; NRHP nomination in preparation.
Hurricane Irma toppled an 'old tower' on Buck Island onto its side (Free Press). The Free Press does not say which tower; see the structures entry.
Coast Guard rebuilt the aid with a 3,500-pound tower; fully operational by early May 2023.

corrections.proposed: historic light inactive; the 2023 tower is an active aid
corrections.why: Rowlett's directory describes the old light as inactive and the new tower as active; the Coast Guard release says the rebuilt light is fully operational.
Kelley's 2003 note says the light was in use until the mid 1990s; the record's 1990 is from Wikidata and is not in the Kelley or Rowlett text.
The 1916 government notice gives the light at N 18 deg 16 min 48 sec, W 64 deg 53 min 36 sec.
42.4 m matches the 2023 tower (139 ft, 42 m, per Rowlett). The historic light's flame was about 38 m (125 ft) in 1916; the 1927 inventory also gives 125 ft.
The 1916 notice gives a visibility of about 17.5 nautical miles for the historic light. The record's 8 nm (source: enc) may describe the current light and needs a Light List check.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Kelley's 2003 note and the USLHS record give 1913 as the year the Danish tower was built. A Danish government notice of 8 June 1916 says the light was erected in 1916 and would be lit on 1 August 1916. The 1927 HELP inventory gives 1 August 1916 as 'first built or established'. The story gives both dates and does not choose between them.

Two different events: the United States acquired the islands in 1917 (Rowlett's Virgin Islands page), and the Harbor Board of St. Thomas conveyed the lighthouse property on 29 July 1919 (Kelley). Kelley's own phrase 'at the time of the transfer ... in 1919' is the island-level transfer as he dates it.

notes_for_editor: 1) Dates conflict: 1913 (Kelley 2003 via Rowlett; USLHS record; French Wikipedia, lead only) vs 1916 (the June 1916 Danish government notice in the St. Croix Avis, which gives lighting on 1 Aug 1916; USLHS HELP 1927 'first built or established' 1 Aug 1916). The Coast Guard Historian's Buck Island article (search snippet only: 'Station Established: 1913 (Danish)', 'First Lit: 1915') could not be read: history.uscg.mil returned 403, and the archived copy came back as compressed data. Check that page directly before settling a 1915 date. 2) The Commissioner's FY1918 list (scan 344, printed p.30) is cited as the tool reads it; the 1922 'Buck Island Light Station' line is on scan 748, which the tool reads as printed p.48; the OCR text places it just after the p.48 header, so confirm the page image before citing 'p. 48' in print. 3) The 1927 HELP report gives the site as 45 acres; Kelley gives 0.92 acres for the tower site. Not resolved. 4) The record's ARLHS VIR002 is attached to St. Thomas here (also in Rowlett's VI page), but the ARLHS page for VIR-002 is 'Buck Island (St. Croix) Light' at about 17 47 N, 64 37 W. Check the ARLHS number before using it. 5) USLHS coordinates in the place record are malformed ('64 deg 88.70 min'), so the 1916 notice's position is used for the proposed correction. 6) The toppled 2017 tower is identified as the mid-1990s tower by inference (VI Free Press 'old tower'; Rowlett's description of the 2023 tower as 'almost identical to an older tower built in the 1990s'). Confirm with the Coast Guard. 7) Flash pattern: the 1916 translation's '3 flashes every 20 seconds' is the reading of the OCR'd translation; the timing numbers are garbled in the OCR and were not used. 8) The Fish and Wildlife Service page did not render in the cache; closure statements come from Rowlett (undated). 9) Wheeling Intelligencer, 14 Apr 1917, p. 11 (George Miner, Charlotte Amalie) says 'the Spaniards' put up the lighthouse; the Danish notice contradicts that, so it is not used. 10) Keepers: none named in any source read; the 1927 inventory gives roles only. 11) Newspaper searches: three Chronicling America searches; the 1916 notice appears in the St. Croix Avis on 21, 24 and 28 June 1916 (the 28 June page has the full translation).
